articles.title: Trillion Case for Medicare for All
articles.author: Farrah Hassen
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. America’s affordability crisis played a major role in this year’s midterm elections — and few things in American life have become more unaffordable than health care. It’s about to get worse as premiums rise and Medicaid cuts from the GOP’s so-called “Big Beautiful Bill” take effect. So if Democrats want to deliver on their promise to make life more affordable, then they must use their new congressional majorities to pass Medicare for All. The United States spends more on health care yet has worse health outcomes than comparable high-income countries. articles.author: Ramzy Baroud
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. On the very morning of last week’s critical US midterm elections, President Donald Trump made what seemed like a shocking announcement: no more aid to Israel. “Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4 billion a year, and we made a deal months ago that we’re stopping,” Trump said . He went on to make two seemingly contradictory assertions: “We won’t be paying Israel” and “We’ll help Israel if they need it.” In truth, this prompted little euphoria among those who have long campaigned against US funding of Israel. articles.title: Reactionary Feminists Offer Bad Solutions to Real Problems
articles.author: Kaja Kröger
articles.content_excerpt: To more and more people, the promises of sex-positive liberal feminism feel empty. The sexual ideas that have dominated feminism in the last two decades — including that sexual liberation always serves women’s interests, that consent is the only relevant sexual ethic, and that consuming porn and buying sex are benign practices like any other — are beginning to ring hollow. In this context, an emergent theoretical strand with the pointed, self-chosen name “reactionary feminism” has drawn considerable attention. It calls into question the liberal assertion that every form of sexual morality is anti-feminist — a view the Left has absorbed in recent decades. articles.title: Nonviolent Communication
articles.author: George Cassidy Payne
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. One night on a suicide prevention chat line, a young man typed a sentence I had seen many times before. “Everyone would be better off without me.” He began listing his failures, one after another, as though presenting evidence in a courtroom. My instinct was to challenge his thinking, offer reassurance, or explain why his conclusion was wrong. I wanted him to understand that his life mattered and that the pain he was experiencing did not tell the whole story. Instead, I paused and wrote: “It sounds like you’ve been carrying an overwhelming sense of failure and loneliness.” There was a long silence. Then he responded: “Yeah. articles.title: We Started the School Year with a March on the Principal
articles.content_excerpt: At Ferndale High School, nestled in a Detroit suburb, one of our most pressing problems is the dilapidated building, built in the 1950s. The outdated heating and cooling systems are prone to classroom floods—in the last nine months I've experienced three. Once boiling hot water sprayed out of the HVAC unit during class, nearly injuring a student. It was late August—our last Sunday night of freedom before our teacher professional development week—when six of my co-workers and I received an email from our principal. articles.title: How Cultural Marxism Became a Right-Wing Obsession
articles.author: A. J. A. Woods
articles.content_excerpt: In December 2021, the term “cultural Marxism” was added to the Oxford English Dictionary . It was, according to the OED , a phrase with a sinister and controversial past. Its etymology could allegedly be traced to 1930s Nazi propaganda; its first recorded English-language use was in a 1938 issue of a British Union of Fascists magazine. Despite its dark history, this expression has recently surged in popularity. College campuses and city streets have been plastered with stickers that urge passersby to “smash” cultural Marxism. Prominent US Republicans, such as Texas Senator Ted Cruz and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, have written book-length polemics to blame America’s decline on cultural Marxist ideologies. articles.title: Lessons from an 85-Day Hotel Strike
articles.author: Diana Varenik and Natascha Elena Uhlmann
articles.content_excerpt: You’d be forgiven for worrying, 12 weeks into a strike, that the boss is hell-bent on waiting you out. But after more than 80 days on the picket line at Seattle’s Embassy Suites by Hilton in Pioneer Square, Aspen Desmarais was undeterred. “I can live on a budget,” she said. “Been doing it since day one.” After 85 days, on September 10, workers won the longest hotel strike in Washington state history. Their union, UNITE HERE Local 8, represents 4,000 hospitality workers in Oregon and Washington. Desmarais, a strike captain and bartender at the hotel, worked to keep others motivated throughout the fight. articles.author: Sean Jacobs
articles.content_excerpt: One of Abdul El-Sayed’s greatest skills is his ability to deploy the language of sports to make his case. His fluency in sports allows him to find common ground with interlocutors and audiences, complicating the stereotype that progressives are anti-sports. What makes him convincing and harder for his opponents to dismiss is that he played competitive team sports: El-Sayed was a hockey goalie in middle school. At Bloomfield Hills High School in the suburbs of Detroit, he played football and lacrosse and wrestled, becoming football team captain. These are sports conservatives embrace or consider quintessentially American. articles.author: Bashir Abu-Manneh
articles.content_excerpt: The parliamentary elections held in Israel on October 27 failed to produce a bloc with the sixty-one seats required to govern on its own. Although it remains in the lead, Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp has fallen from sixty-eight to fifty-three seats, while the opposition, led by Gadi Eisenkot, has made gains but secured only forty-eight seats. The two Palestinian lists achieved a historic breakthrough, winning nineteen seats, thanks to an unprecedented mobilization of Palestinian citizens of Israel. Coalition negotiations remain deadlocked, however, as the opposition is reluctant to accept any form of cooperation with the Palestinian parties. articles.author: Nick Couldry
articles.content_excerpt: This September, some rather technical issues regarding artificial intelligence, or rather their upshot, made headlines. The reason lay in two resignations from companies leading the development of frontier AI models, namely David Robinson , OpenAI’s Safety Officer, and Jacob Coxon , a developer at Anthropic. Each resigned because they no longer believed the companies were taking seriously the risks that frontier models’ recent “advances” pose to the survival of humanity . So, not just what most of us would call a “technical issue.” Those fears were not hype. articles.title: Kurds Have Become Britain’s Latest Demonized Migrants
articles.author: Matt Broomfield
articles.content_excerpt: A decade ago, the Kurds briefly figured in Western public consciousness as the feted heroes of the war against the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria (ISIS). In Britain as worldwide, audiences were fascinated by fetishized, orientalized images of “badass” Kurdish female fighters battling the Islamist terror group on the ground, backed by the UK and US militaries. Today the most populous stateless people in the Middle East are making headlines in the UK once again, but this time depicted as people smugglers, organized criminals, and unwanted illegal immigrants. Broadly speaking, both migrants themselves and the smuggling networks who profit from their need to travel are hysterically depicted as united in highly organized, criminal, Islamic gangs that need to be “smashed” by the UK government.

Goldie Taylor, 80, and I grew up in small-town Mayfield, Kentucky, when Jim Crow segregation and race discrimination were both the law and the social order. I’m 76. Symbolic of the separate and unequal order, mayors were white men. “I never believed it would change,” said Taylor, who is my longtime friend and president of our Mayfield-Graves County NAACP branch. “I never dreamed we could ever have a Black mayor in the city of Mayfield.” Neither did I.
